thread:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] kv-cache amplification detected in prod-east for continuous batching. latency p95↑, write amplification x10 for tenant acme-corp-42. paging @Anna

Anna (oncall): I'm on it. Dashboards show continuous_batch queue length spiking around 11:04 UTC, KV write rate and hotset growth correlates. Loading logs now.

Jordan (eng-runtime): I see a correlated perf cliff after the batch_window_v2 rollout yesterday. Some requests are triggering very long prefix scans, causing large KV entries to be created. Not all tenants affected, looks concentrated on acme-corp-42 and a few adjacent shards.

Lee (sre): Any recent deploys to runtime or kernel changes?

Jordan (eng-runtime): No runtime deploys in the last 12h. We did flip batch_window_v2 from default=legacy to default=v2 for new customers; config was supposed to be opt-in per-tenant but a service bug flipped the default for some shards.

Maria (support): Support tickets: acme-corp-42 reported increased 500s and timeouts ~11:10. They're seeing stuck LLM responses. They're flagged as high-priority customer.

Anna (oncall): Impact assessment: 1 tenant (acme-corp-42) high, ~4 tenants medium. System-wide latency elevated but not fully saturated yet. Suggest hotfix path: per-customer override for acme-corp-42 immediate, then canary rollback of batch_window_v2 defaults while we fix config migration.

Sam (platform): Agreed. We should avoid a global flag-off unless traffic indicates broader risk. Per-tenant override available via feature flags. I can push a per-customer toggle.

Jordan (eng-runtime): Steps I propose:
1) Apply per-tenant override for acme-corp-42 to revert to legacy batching.
2) Run a 5% global canary rollback of batch_window_v2 to check for latent regressions.
3) If stable, roll back defaults back to legacy for affected shard range.

Anna (oncall): Execute step 1 now please. Sam, can you run the override? Link to flag UI: <https://flags.redwood.internal/flags/batch_window_v2>

Sam (platform): Running CLI to set per-tenant override:
`/feature-flag set batch_window_v2 legacy --tenant acme-corp-42 --by sam --reason "mitigate kv cache amplification"`

Sam (platform): Patch applied, propagating. Watching KV write rate and cache occupancy.

oncall-bot: Feature flag change detected: batch_window_v2 -> legacy for tenant acme-corp-42 (actor: Sam).

Jordan (eng-runtime): Early signals look good — KV write rate for that tenant dropped ~70% within 45s. Continuous batch queue draining.

Maria (support): Let me update acme-corp-42 support channel: "We applied a targeted rollback for you; please validate if things look back to normal on your side."

Anna (oncall): Good. Next, prepare global canary rollback. Decide canary percent + duration? I suggest 5% traffic for 15 minutes with quick AB metrics on kv-write-rate and p95 latency.

Lee (sre): 5% seems safe. I'll set an automated abort if kv-write-rate or p95 latency regresses more than 15% vs baseline. Also ensure alerting unmuted for the canary window.

Sam (platform): Initiating rollout: `/feature-rollout start batch_window_v2 --variant legacy --percent 5 --duration 15m --monitor "kv.write_rate,p95_latency"`

oncall-bot: Rollout started: batch_window_v2 legacy @ 5% for 15m. Canary monitor configured (abort threshold: 15% regression).

Jordan (eng-runtime): T+3m into canary: no regressions observed in the canary slice. KV write-rate stable, p95 slightly improved for canary traffic.

Anna (oncall): Ok. Keep the canary running. Meanwhile, Jordan, please audit the config migration path that flipped defaults for shards — that's the root cause.

Jordan (eng-runtime): On it. Early hypothesis: migration job wrote default flag to shard metadata; a race allowed some shard leaders to pick up v2. I'll add a fail-safe check and a dry-run for future migrations.

Maria (support): acme-corp-42 confirmed recovery at 11:25 — responses normal, 500s dropped. They're happy but asking for RCA and timeline.

Lee (sre): After the 15m canary completes, if still clean, we should schedule a controlled rollback for the affected shard range rather than flipping global defaults. Also prepare postmortem stub.

Sam (platform): Canary completed: no abort. Rolling plan: batch_window_v2 defaults will be set to legacy for shard-range s-102..s-110 and we'll run a migration fix. Triggering per-shard override now to be safe.

Sam (platform): Command: `/feature-flag set batch_window_v2 legacy --shard-range s-102:s-110 --by sam --reason "mitigate accidental default flip"`

oncall-bot: Flag update: per-shard overrides applied for s-102..s-110.

Anna (oncall): Handoff — I'm going offline for a scheduled rotation at 12:00 UTC. Handing to Lee for ongoing monitoring and RCA coordination. Lee, can you take point on the postmortem and communicate timeline to acme-corp-42?

Lee (sre): Taking handoff. I'll own the postmortem and customer comms. Preliminary RCA: config-migration bug + missing shard leader guard caused batch defaults to flip; mitigated by per-tenant/shard overrides. I'll follow up with timeline and action items.

Anna (oncall): Thanks. Slack thread will be the source of truth. If anything regresses, re-paging. :thumbsup:

Maria (support): I'll file the customer update and include rollback details.

Jordan (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR with the migration fix + automated canary for migrations.

Lee (sre): Closing live mitigation stage. We'll convert this into a postmortem link once the doc is ready.

oncall-bot: Incident closed (mitigated): kv-cache amplification for acme-corp-42. Severity lowered to S2.
